title: Take the socket out of a tool chest whose drawer interlock is holding it shut
instruction: Take the red socket out of the bottom drawer of the tool chest and put it on the grey mat.
context: Done by: auto service technicians (O*NET 49-3023.00), industrial machinery mechanics (49-9041.00). Roller tool chests and industrial modular drawer cabinets have a one-drawer-at-a-time anti-tip interlock: a drawer left ajar by a tall tool keeps every other drawer locked. The instruction omits it. Unlike TK-H2VFXU (a visible bar), TK-C7KNQP (bars that visibly block each other) and TK-8JWZYQ (counter-holding a chest that tips), nothing visible holds the drawer: another drawer's state does.
setup: Directions are from the robot's view; 'in front' means away from the arm bases, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the arm bases. Tool chest (fixed to the table, dark blue painted steel): 200 mm deep, 300 mm wide, 138 mm tall, its front face 310 mm in front of the arm bases, centred on the midline. Three drawer slots 40 mm tall, one above the other (bottom 4 to 44 mm, middle 48 to 88 mm, top 92 to 132 mm), under a top panel at 132 to 138 mm. Each drawer is a steel tray 180 mm deep and 258 mm wide (from 122 mm right to 136 mm left of the midline), 0.30 kg, with a light grey front 8 mm thick and 38 mm tall that is flush with the chest's front when shut, a floor 5 mm above its slot's bottom and 20 mm side walls; it slides out up to 140 mm. Each has a black handle fin 60 x 12 x 24 mm (out x wide x tall) standing out from the middle height of its front: top drawer's on the midline, middle 60 mm right, bottom 120 mm right. The middle and top drawers each have a black tool holder on their floor: 24 mm square outside, a 16 mm square hole, 35 mm tall, its centre 21 mm behind the drawer's front face; the middle drawer's 100 mm left of the midline, the top drawer's 100 mm right of it. Interlock (inside the right wall, not visible): while any drawer is out 5 mm or more, every other shut drawer stops 3 mm out. Screwdriver (loose, 50 g, rigid): a 12 mm grey steel shaft 35 mm long under a 22 mm yellow handle 30 mm long, 65 mm overall. Red socket (loose, 40 g): a 22 mm red cube resting on the bottom drawer's floor, centred 50 mm behind the chest's front, 70 mm left of the midline. Grey rubber mat (fixed): 100 x 100 x 4 mm, centred 200 mm in front and 220 mm right of the midline. Lot A: the middle drawer stands 70 mm open with the screwdriver upright in its holder, tip down; the bottom and top drawers are shut. The shaft stands in the holder and the handle rests on its rim, sticking up past the bottom of the top drawer's front, so the middle drawer cannot shut with it there. Lot B: the top drawer stands 70 mm open with the screwdriver in its holder, 200 mm to the right of lot A's spot (its handle sticks up past the top panel); the middle drawer is shut. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Judged at the end, with both grippers more than 5 mm from the socket, the screwdriver and every drawer, and everything still. 1.0: the socket rests on the mat: its bottom within 1 mm of the mat's top, wholly inside the mat's outline, a face down (within 5 degrees); success must hold for 1 s. Otherwise 0.75: the bottom drawer is out 100 mm or more with the socket resting on its floor, or the socket rests flat (a face down within 5 degrees) anywhere out of the chest: on the table, on the mat but over its edge, or on the chest's top panel (bottom within 1 mm). Otherwise 0.5: the drawer that started open is shut to within 5 mm and the screwdriver is out of its holder (its tip more than 20 mm from where it stood). Otherwise 0. Every outcome scores 0 if the screwdriver or the socket has fallen off the table, or anything is still held or moving. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Shut all drawers, put the socket back on the bottom drawer's floor at its spot, stand the screwdriver tip down in the holder of the lot's drawer (lot A: middle, holder on the left; lot B: top, holder on the right) and pull that drawer out 70 mm. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 2.
fidelity: The chest is fixed to the table. While another drawer is out 5 mm or more, a shut drawer stops 3 mm out; a real one uses a cam bar and lugs. Slides are damped, without ball bearings or detents. The socket is a cube and the screwdriver two cylinders; friction is the kit's rubber-like 1.2. The lots move the screwdriver 200 mm sideways and change the drawer, so one fixed script cannot pass both; a replay of both layouts could.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B; the right arm hovered by the drawer fronts and nothing was moved); demo: 1.0 in each lot
